title: Blichfeldt's Strengthening of Minkowski
content: Hans Blichfeldt's 1914 theorem replaces Minkowski's geometric hypotheses (convex, centrally symmetric) with a single measure-theoretic one: vol(S) > k already forces k+1 points of S that are pairwise ℤⁿ-congruent. The proof is a fundamental-domain pigeonhole, flexible enough that Minkowski's classical theorem falls out as a corollary via the half-scaling T = (1/2)·S. This formalization is axiom-free (status `verified`): the module docstring records that all four originally-stated axioms were eliminated across sessions S1–S14 — the k=1 case now calls Mathlib's `IsAddFundamentalDomain.exists_ne_zero_vadd_eq` directly, and the general-k case `blichfeldt_general` was promoted from axiom to a fully proved theorem (PRs #17298/#17329).
mathContext:
**k=1**: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > 1 \Rightarrow \exists\, x \ne y \in S,\ x - y \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.

**general**: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > k \Rightarrow \exists\ k{+}1$ distinct $x_0,\dots,x_k \in S$ with all $x_i - x_j \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.

title: Measure-Theory Infrastructure (Proved, Not Axioms)
content: Two proved helper theorems (both were axioms in earlier sessions). `blichfeldt_proj_measurable`: the slice {z ∈ F | z+v ∈ S} is measurable, since translation z ↦ z+v is measurable (`measurable_id.add_const`) so the preimage is measurable, intersected with the measurable fundamental domain. `blichfeldt_disj_bound`: pairwise-disjoint measurable subsets of F have total volume ≤ 1, via `measure_iUnion` (σ-additivity) + `measure_mono` against `stdLattice_covolume = 1`. These are kept as reusable building blocks for the general-k covering-count argument.
mathContext: $\{z \in F \mid z+v \in S\} = F \cap (\cdot + v)^{-1}(S)$ is measurable; $\sum'_v \mathrm{vol}(A_v) = \mathrm{vol}(\bigcup_v A_v) \le \mathrm{vol}(F) = 1$ for pairwise-disjoint $A_v \subseteq F$.

title: Blichfeldt's Basic Theorem k=1 (Proved, Axiom-Free)
content: `blichfeldt_basic`: a measurable S ⊆ ℝⁿ with vol(S) > 1 contains two distinct points x, y with x − y ∈ ℤⁿ. The current proof is a direct application of Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.IsAddFundamentalDomain.exists_ne_zero_vadd_eq` to the standard ℤⁿ-fundamental-domain (covolume 1): a set of volume > 1 cannot avoid all lattice translates, yielding x, y ∈ S with g +ᵥ x = y for some g ≠ 0; the `g +ᵥ x = y` AddSubgroup action is bridged to (g:ℝⁿ)+x = y via `AddSubgroup.vadd_def`/`vadd_eq_add`. The `[NeZero n]` instance rules out the vacuous ℝ⁰ case.
mathContext: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > 1 \Rightarrow \exists\, x, y \in S,\ x \ne y,\ x - y \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. Earlier proofs built the pigeonhole by hand from a `blichfeldt_volume_partition` axiom (now eliminated).

title: Covering-Count Integral Identity
content: The analytic core for the general-k case. `volume_eq_setLIntegral_indicator_tsum` proves the covering-count identity ∫⁻ z in F, c(z) dz = vol(S), where c(z) = ∑' v∈ℤⁿ, 1_S((v:ℝⁿ)+z) counts how many lattice translates of z land in S. It follows from Mathlib's `IsAddFundamentalDomain.lintegral_eq_tsum''` plus Tonelli (to swap the ℕ∞-valued sum and integral). `volume_eq_setLIntegral_indicator_tsum_lattice` is the basis-parametric variant for an arbitrary full-rank ℤ-lattice. This replaces the old 'averaging argument — currently axiomatized' with a proved identity.
mathContext: $\int_F c(z)\, dz = \sum_{v\in\mathbb{Z}^n} \mathrm{vol}(S_v) = \mathrm{vol}(S)$, with $c(z) = \#\{v : z+v \in S\}$ — averaging then forces $c(z) \ge k+1$ somewhere when $\mathrm{vol}(S) > k$.

title: Blichfeldt's General Theorem (Proved via Path A Contrapose)
content: `blichfeldt_general`: vol(S) > k yields k+1 pairwise ℤⁿ-congruent points — promoted from axiom to a fully proved theorem (S13/S14). The proof is a contrapositive in three moves. Move A: rewrite vol(S) as ∫_F c(z) dz via the covering-count identity. Move B: from the negation of the conclusion, derive the pointwise bound c(z) ≤ k, rewriting the tsum-of-indicators as the encard of the hitting set T(z) (`tsum_subtype` + `ENNReal.tsum_set_one`) and extracting a `Fin (k+1) → L` injection from the encard bound (`Set.toFinset_card` + `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`). Move C: integrate c(z) ≤ k over F (`setLIntegral_mono_ae` + `setLIntegral_const` + covolume 1) to get vol(S) ≤ k, contradicting the hypothesis.
mathContext: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > k \Rightarrow \exists$ injective $x : \mathrm{Fin}(k+1) \to S$ with all $x_i - x_j \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. Contradiction: $c(z) \le k$ everywhere would give $\mathrm{vol}(S) = \int_F c \le k$.

title: General Theorem for an Arbitrary Full-Rank Lattice
content: `blichfeldt_general_lattice` generalizes from the standard lattice ℤⁿ to any full-rank ℤ-lattice L: if vol(S) > k · covol(L) then S has k+1 points pairwise congruent mod L. `blichfeldt_basic_from_general` then recovers the k=1 case from the general theorem (a consistency cross-check, extracting two points indexed by `Fin 2`). The lattice-parametric form is the version most useful downstream, where lattices arise with covolume ≠ 1.
mathContext: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > k\cdot\mathrm{covol}(L) \Rightarrow \exists\ k{+}1$ points of $S$ pairwise congruent mod $L$.

title: Concrete and Reformulated Blichfeldt Corollaries
content: Named specializations and alternative phrasings, all proved. `blichfeldt_three_points` (k=2: vol > 2 ⇒ 3 congruent points) and `blichfeldt_four_points` (k=3: vol > 3 ⇒ 4 points) instantiate the general theorem at small k. `blichfeldt_general_pairwise` restates the conclusion with explicit nonzero pairwise differences (the classical 'there exist distinct points whose differences are nonzero lattice vectors' phrasing). `blichfeldt_general_finset` packages the k+1 witnesses as a `Finset` of cardinality k+1 rather than a `Fin (k+1)` indexing — the form convenient for counting applications.
mathContext: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > 2 \Rightarrow 3$ congruent points; $\mathrm{vol}(S) > 3 \Rightarrow 4$; pairwise/Finset forms repackage the same $k{+}1$ witnesses.

title: Minkowski Recovered via Half-Scaling (Sorry-Free)
content: `minkowski_from_blichfeldt` derives Minkowski's classical lattice-point theorem from `blichfeldt_basic`, with 0 sorries (was 2). Set T = (1/2)·S; then vol(T) = vol(S)/2ⁿ > 1 when vol(S) > 2ⁿ, so Blichfeldt gives a ≠ b ∈ T with a − b ∈ ℤⁿ. Writing a = x₀/2, b = y₀/2: central symmetry of S gives −y₀ ∈ S, and convexity gives the midpoint (x₀ + (−y₀))/2 = a − b ∈ S — a nonzero lattice point. The two formerly-sorried facts are now proved: measurability of T (rewrite as preimage of S under the doubling map) and the volume identity (`Measure.addHaar_smul` + ENNReal arithmetic on (2⁻¹)ⁿ·2ⁿ = 1). Convexity converting a *difference* in T into a *single element* of S is precisely why Blichfeldt is strictly stronger than Minkowski.
mathContext: $\mathrm{vol}(S) > 2^n,\ S$ convex & centrally symmetric $\Rightarrow \exists\, 0 \ne p \in S \cap \mathbb{Z}^n$, via $T = \tfrac12 S$ and $a - b = \tfrac12(x_0 + (-y_0)) \in S$.

title: Generalized Minkowski (k+1-Point Forms)
content: The k+1-point generalizations of Minkowski, all proved by combining `blichfeldt_general` with the half-scaling and convexity/symmetry extraction. `minkowski_general_k`: a convex centrally-symmetric S with vol(S) > k·2ⁿ contains k+1 lattice points (the standard counting strengthening). `minkowski_general_k_pairwise` states it with explicit nonzero pairwise differences, and `minkowski_general_k_finset` packages the witnesses as a Finset of size k+1. `minkowski_four_points` is the concrete k=3 instance. These mirror the Blichfeldt corollary family, transported through the half-scaling bridge.
mathContext: $S$ convex, centrally symmetric, $\mathrm{vol}(S) > k\cdot 2^n \Rightarrow |S \cap \mathbb{Z}^n| \ge k+1$ (counting form of Minkowski).
